broadshoulderedbastard: Hugo "Lucky" Broadshoulde came up the line with a photograph gone soft at the edges and nothing else. The sergeant wrote him down as Private and pointed at the mud.
Hugo "Lucky" Broadshoulde began repairing a blanket with scraps from ruined clothing. The first patch is a different colour from everything else.

A shell landed square in S-F20. They found Hugo "Lucky" Broadshoulde alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. Hugo "Lucky" Broadshoulde died at his post at S-F20 when the dugout roof came down under a direct hit.
Rafael Broadshoulde came to the front because his uncle Hugo "Lucky" Broadshoulde never came home. He carries a photograph gone soft at the edges.
ethanbay_23: Wendel "Parson" Ethanbay arrived with the evening ration party, carrying his mother's thimble and a borrowed coat two sizes too big.

A shell landed square in S-S9. They found Wendel "Parson" Ethanbay alive under the sandbags, barely. Every minute counts now. Wendel "Parson" Ethanbay was killed outright by a direct hit at S-S9. The men dug for an hour and found only his identity disc.
The House of Ethanbay sent another. Hugo "Button" Ethanbay, older brother of Wendel "Parson" Ethanbay, arrived with the same eyes and the same stubborn silence.
zczc1317: Nils Zczc left a girl from the dance hall, maybe behind in Millbank and came up the line with a bullet that missed him. The men noticed at once that he never sits with his back to the parapet.
The colonel shook hands with the first hundred, one by one. Nils Zczc was number 91. He still remembers how cold the colonel's glove was.
Day 3. The Concord took Verdel Ridge. From the heights Nils Zczc could see the whole Hegemony line, and for the first time the war looked winnable.
A bullet went through Nils Zczc's sleeve at S-F9 and took some skin with it. He kept the sleeve. Shot by Cyril Mateorekon of the Hegemony (@mateorekon).
Stitches out, sleeve rolled down. Nils Zczc is whole again, or near enough for the line.
Nils Zczc lifted the trench periscope and found a spider across the mirror. For one startled second, the enemy seemed enormous.
